Winning and Losing
If any player loses, then the game ends immediately. If you do not lose and your opponent does, then you win the game.
If any player fulfils any losing conditions during a check timing (11.6.1), then that player loses Action).
If a player has six or more cards in their damage zone, then he or she fulfills a losing condition.
If a player has no cards in their deck, then he or she fulfills a losing condition.
If a player has no vanguards on their vanguard circle, and has no cards in their soul, then he or she fulfills a losing condition.
If all players lose simultaneously, then the game ends in a draw.
Any player may declare their concession at any time. The player who declared their concession immediately loses without proceeding to the check timing (11.6.1), and the game ends.
No effects can interfere with conceding. No effects can force a player to concede, and no effects can replace losing the game with a concession.

There are cards with effects that have a player win or lose the game. In these cases, that player wins or loses while resolving the effect without proceeding to the check timing (11.6.1), and the game ends. card contradict with each other, then the text takes precedence.

If anything attempts to make a player do something he or she cannot perform, then nothing happens. If anything attempts to make a player do something he or she can only partially perform, then the player only performs the part that he or she can.
If anything attempts to turn a game state into a state that it is already in, then it does not become the state again, and that action never happens.
If anything attempts to perform a certain action zero or a negative number of times, then nothing happens. No reverse action will take place even if it is a negative number of times.

If anything attempts to perform actions that are being done as part of the cost of a card, ability, or effect, zero or a negative number of times, you can choose to do those actions as part of the cost, and that part of the cost is considered to be performed without anything being performed as a result.

When performing an action, if there is an instruction to perform a process a specified number of times “(as much) as possible”, the number of times the player performing the process chooses to perform the process needs to be as close to the specified number as possible.

If an effect has an instruction to perform a process a specified number of times “(as much) as possible”, and it cannot be performed the specified number of times because of a card’s information that is hidden from any player, that card’s information must be revealed to all players. - For example, if there is an instruction to perform a “call a card from your hand to a rear-guard circle as much as possible” effect, if there are cards in your hand that can be called to rear-guard circles, and cards that cannot be called, you need to choose a card that can be called. On the other hand, if all the cards in your hand cannot be called, you need to reveal them.
If an effect from a card attempts to do something, and at the same time an effect from a card restricts the action from taking place, then the effect that restricts the action takes precedence.

If anything asks more than one player to make a choice at the same time, then the turn player makes the choice first. The non-turn player will make their choice after knowing the decision made by the turn player.

If more than one player is to make a choice of cards in a hidden zone at the same time, the turn player first chooses the required number of cards without checking their information, followed by the non-turn player choosing the required number of cards. If the chosen cards are to be revealed, it is done after both players have made their choices.
If anything asks a player to choose a number, then you must choose zero or a positive integer, if not specified. You cannot choose any fractions or negative numbers.
If a number is specified for the upper limit in a form such as “up to X”, unless a number is specified for the lower limit, you can choose zero.

When a numerical value is changed to be greater than its current value by a rule or effect, that value is considered to have increased. Similarly, if a value is changed to be less than its current value, that value is considered to have decreased.

When there is an instruction to “increase” a value, and the resulting value after carrying out that instruction is less than before the effect was applied, that value is considered to have decreased instead of increasing, and similarly for the reverse.
When an object such as a player or a card starts an action, the following events occur in according to the content of that action.
If an object A performs a single action X, an “A did X” event occurs.

If an object A starts an action X that is continuously performed, an “A did X” event occurs, and an “A is doing X” state is maintained while X is being performed. - For example, when a rear-guard attacks, the “rear-guard attacks” event occurs, and the “rear-guard is attacking” state is maintained until the end of that battle.

If an object A starts an action X that is continuously performed on object B, the “A did X to B” and “X was done to B by A” events occur, and the “A is doing X to B” and “X is being done to B by A” states are maintained while X is being performed. - For example, when a vanguard attacks a rear-guard, the “vanguard attacks a rear- guard” and “rear-guard is attacked by a vanguard” events occur, and the “vanguard is attacking a rear-guard” and “rear-guard is being attacked by a vanguard” states are maintained until the end of that battle.

With regards to 1.3.7.2 and 1.3.7.3, even if the action that was continuously being performed has ended, the “did” event that occurred at its start is not canceled. - For example, if a rear-guard in the back row boosts a vanguard in the front row, even if that rear-guard is later moved to another circle during that battle and loses its “is boosting” state, the “this unit boosted” event is not canceled.
Name
The inherent name to identify a card.
Some Japanese cards have small letters above the name to help show how to read it. This is not a part of the name and has no
In text, the name of a card may be expressed as “(card name)“ or “(part of a card name)”, depending on the context.

There are some cards with a “This card is also regarded as “(card name)” continuous ability that does not specify a zone. This ability is active in all zones (11.4), and is referenced as a card with each of those names when constructing a deck (8.1.5.2).
Clan
The name of the clan a card belongs to.
The clan is referred to by some abilities and effects.
In text, the name of a clan or nation may be expressed as <<(name)>>.
“This card is also a <<( name)>>“ is an effect that adds a clan or nation to the card with the ability.
<<Cray Elemental>> cards belong to all clans and nations.
Order cards without any clan or nation belong to all clans and nations.
Race
The name of the race of a card.
The race is referred to by some abilities and effects.
In text, the name of a race may be expressed as <(race name)>.
There are cards that have multiple races. In such cases, the names of each race are demarcated by “/”.
Grade
The numeric value that is referred to when you ride or call a card.
The grade can limit the playing of a card.
Power
The numeric value that expresses the combat strength of a card. The higher this value is, the better it is in battle.
In text, the word “power” may be indicated by a icon.
Some cards have a “+“ after the numerical
Shield
The numeric value that expresses this card’s combat strength as a guardian (10.5.1.2.2). The higher this value is, the better it is at defending your units.
In text, the shield may be indicated by a icon.
Some units do not have a shield.
Critical
The numeric value that determines how much damage this card deals to the opponent’s vanguard in battle.
In text, the critical may be indicated by a icon.
Trigger Icon
The icon that indicates the trigger ability (11.10.1) to be played when instructed by cards
Type
The information about the type of a card.
Cards can have 3 different type information: main type, subtype, and special type.
Generally, all cards have a main type and a subtype.
There are some pseudo-cards (15.1.2.4) that have a special type.
Cards have one out of the “unit”, “order”, “heart”, “originalDress”, “crest”, or “ride deck crest” main types.

“Unit” is a general term for cards that are placed on the field and battle with the opponent or support such battles. to a “unit” without specifying a zone, they are referring to a card on the field (4.8) with the main type “unit”.
“Order” is a general term for cards that only have abilities that support units or players.
“Heart” is the main type cards in the heart state (6.5.2.2) have.
“originalDress” is the main type cards in the “originalDress” state (6.7.2.1) have.
“Crest” is the card type that “crest” pseudo- cards (15.7) have.
“Ride deck crest” is a general term for cards added to the ride deck during deck construction (8.1.2).
Cards may have subtypes according to their main type.
Cards with the “heart” and “originalDress” main types maintain their original subtype.
There are some cards and pseudo-cards (15.1.2.4) that have a special type.
Special types are different from and independent of types. Effects that add, remove, or change types do not affect special types, and vice versa.

Card types are written as a combination of the subtype and main type. - For example, the type of a card with main type “unit” and subtype “trigger” is written as “trigger unit”.
Skill Icon
An icon that indicates one of the abilities that card has.
Cards with the icon have “Boost” (14.5).
Cards with the icon have “Intercept” (14.4).
Cards with the icon have “Twin Drive!!“ (14.3.3).
Cards with the icon have “Triple Drive!!!“ (14.3.4).
Card Text
The information about a card’s inherent abilities.
The content within the frame may be referred to as “text“.
Some text is colored differently to put an emphasis on it. The difference in colors has no

Some cards have text in ( ) (brackets) to indicate an explanation of an ability. This is called reminder text. Reminder text is part of the text, but as it is only for explanatory purposes, it does not affect the game.
Flavor
The descriptive text of this card.
Special Icon
Cards with specific icons in this position have an ability that corresponds with the icon.
If this card has one of the following icons, it has an imaginary gift (16.1).
This card has the imaginary gift of the following clan types (16.2.1.1) that corresponds with the icon.
Cards with the icon to the right have the clan type “Force” imaginary gift.
Cards with the icon to the right have the clan type “Accel” imaginary gift.
Cards with the icon to the right have the clan type “Protect” imaginary gift.
If this card has the icon to the right, it means that this card can perform Persona Ride (6.3.8).
Nation
The name of the nation a card belongs to.
The nation is referred to by some abilities and effects.
Nations are represented by nation names and their nation icons.
When nations are only represented by their nation icon, they have the following meaning.

Some specific nations are also considered to be other specified nations. In addition, cards with nation names or icons that have no indication of belonging to any specific clan in their card information are considered to belong to all the clans that correspond to that nation.
Please refer to supplement B at the end of this document for a list of nations and their corresponding clans.
Nation names may be referenced as <<(nation name)>> in text (2.2.3).
Art
The descriptive image of this card.
Collection Data

The card’s collection number, artist’s name, copyright, and other contents of the card with no direct relation to game that have not been mentioned thus far are collectively called the “collection data”.
The collection data is not part of the information of this card and generally have no
There are some effects that refer to the collection number during deck construction (8.1.8).
Drive
The numeric value that determines the number of drive checks resolved during the battle that a card attacked.
The drive is not indicated on a card, and the original value for all cards is 1.
Cards with the “Twin Drive!!” or “Triple Drive!!!” skill icons have the value of their drive changed by those abilities.
Player
The player (or “fighter“) is a person playing the game.
Each player has a “vanguard damage” value that is incurred when their vanguard receives damage.
Each player has an “energy” value that is referenced by some cards.
The lower limit for energy is 0. While energy would usually have no upper limit, an upper limit may be set by effects.
Owner and Master

The owner is the player who owns the card. The owner of a card is the player who had it in their deck at the beginning of the game. At the end of each game, each player retrieves each card that he or she owns.
The master is the player who is currently using a card, ability, or effects. The master of a card in a zone is the player whom the zone belongs to.
The master of a continuous ability is the master of the card that has that ability, or the master of an effect that created that ability.
The master of an activated ability is the player who played it.
The master of an automatic ability is the master of the card that has that ability, or the master of an effect that created that ability.
The master of an order ability is the master of the order card with that ability.
The master of an effect is the master of the ability that generated that effect.
If an effect instructs for any actions to be performed without specifying a player, the master of that effect carries out those instructions.
Zone Basics
For each zone, each player has their own one if not specified.

There are zones where all players may see the information of the cards in that zone, and zones where they may not. Zones in which information of the cards in that zone may be seen are “public zones”, and zones in which they may not are called “hidden zones”.
When a card is placed in a public zone, it is placed in the public state (4.2.2). When a card is placed in a hidden zone, it is placed in the hidden state (4.2.3).
All players may check the number of cards in any zone at any time, regardless of whether the zone is public or hidden.

Generally, even when a card in a public zone is turned face down by a rule or card’s effect, all players may see the information of that card. Generally, while a card in a hidden zone is revealed, all players may see the information of that card.

When a card would move from a hidden zone to a public zone or change state within the zone, if any effect restricts the moving or changing of state of that card due to that card’s information, that card is revealed.

There are zones where the order cards are placed in the zone is controlled. If the order is controlled, the order the cards are stacked on each other is controlled. Unless otherwise specified, players cannot change the order of cards in a zone where the order is controlled.
When a card is moved to a zone where the order is not controlled, after indicating that that card is moving to that zone, that card can be moved to any position in that zone.

When a card moves from a circle to another circle, it is considered as the same card as the original card, and the effects that applied to the original card continue to apply. However, when performing a move from a circle to a zone other than a circle, unless otherwise specified, it is considered as a new card in the new zone. Effects that applied in the previous zone do not continue to apply.
When a single card effect moves a card to another zone and performs an action on the card in the zone it moved to, that effect tracks the card after it has moved, and performs the action.
When multiple cards are placed in a zone at the same time, unless otherwise specified, the order they are placed in the new zone is decided by the owner of that zone.

When multiple cards are placed from a public zone into a hidden zone at the same time, and the master of those cards can determine the order those cards are placed, no player other than the master may know the order those cards are placed.
When cards are moved to a specific position in a hidden zone, the number of cards moved to that position is known to all players.
When instructed to move a card would move to a zone whose master is not specified, unless otherwise specified, move it to the specified zone of that card’s owner.
When a card would be moved to the zone of a player other than that card’s owner, unless particularly specified by a rule or effect, that move is not performed.
Zone Visibility State
Cards in zones have either the public state or hidden state.
All players may see the information of cards in the public state.
Some or all players may not see the information of cards in the hidden state.
Card Placement State
It is possible for the card placement state to be specified in some zones. The placement states are the orientation state, and the facing state.
The orientation state can either be the “stand state” or the “rest state”. Cards can only have one of the two orientation states, and cannot be in both or neither of the states.
Cards in the stand state are placed vertically upright from its master’s viewpoint. In card text, “stand” may be indicated by a icon.
Cards in the rest state are placed horizontally from its master’s viewpoint. In card text, “rest” may be indicated by a icon.
When a card is placed in a zone where it is possible for the placement state to be specified, unless otherwise specified, it is placed in the stand state.
The facing state can either be “face up” or “face down”. A card can only have one of the two facing states, and cannot be in both or neither of the states.
Cards in the face up state are placed such that the face with the card information is visible. Generally, all players may check the information of face up cards.
Cards in the face down state are placed such that the face with the card information is not visible. Generally, no player may check the information of face down cards.

Generally, cards placed face up are in the public state, and cards placed in the public state are placed face up. Similarly, cards placed face down are in the hidden state, and cards placed in the hidden state are placed face down.
Card Types and Movement to Zones of cards with specific main types or subtypes to specific zones.

When a card with the subtype “G” performs a move between zones that is not a movement from striding (6.5.1), or a movement from a rear- guard circle or vanguard circle to a rear-guard circle, in the following situations, that card moves to the G zone.
If that card is the vanguard, and would move to another zone, it is placed face up in the G zone instead of performing that move.
If that card is a rear-guard, after performing that move, it is immediately placed in the G zone face up from the zone it had moved to without waiting for the check timing.
When a card with the main type “order” would move to any circle, it is placed in the drop zone instead of performing that move.
Deck Zone
The zone you put your deck in at the beginning of a game.

The deck zone is a hidden zone, and the order of the cards is controlled. Players can only change the order of the cards in the deck, or check the information of those cards, if an effect or rule instructs them to.
When multiple cards move from the deck zone to another zone at the same time, move cards one by one.
Hand
The zone where each player places their unused cards without letting the opponent see them.
The hand is a hidden zone, but you can see information of cards in your hand. You may not see information of cards in your opponent’s hand. The order of the cards in the hand is not controlled.
Drop Zone
The zone where each player places cards that have been used.
The drop zone is a public zone. Cards in this zone are stacked face up, and the information of cards are open to all players. The order of the cards in the drop zone is not controlled.
When text refers to “drop”, it refers to the drop zone.
Field
The zone to put all your units on.
In general, this zone has seven circles. A card on a circle is also regarded as being on the field that the circle belongs to.
The field is a public zone.
Circle
The zone to put your unit on individually. Each player has 7 circles: left front, center front, right front, left back, center back, right back, and center far front.
Each pair of circles, left front and left back, center front and center back, and right front and right back, is called a column.

Your opponent's column directly across your own column is the same column. Specifically, your left column and your opponent's right column, your center column and your opponent's center column, your right column and your opponent's left column, are the same columns.
All the circles in a player’s front row, and all the circles in a player’s back row, are each called a row.
Circles on the field have 1 of the following types, namely “Vanguard“, “Rear-guard“, “Guardian“, “Lock“, “Astral Plane”, or “Stage”.
A circle with a type will have the name of “(type) circle“. - For example, a circle with the Vanguard type is called a “Vanguard circle”.
Cards placed on circles have an orientation state.
The type of the center front circle at the beginning of the game is a vanguard type.
When a card is put on the vanguard circle from anywhere other than by striding (6.5.1), including a rear-guard circle, it is put there in the stand state.
The type of the center far front circle at the beginning of the game is a guardian type.
When a card is placed on this zone, unless otherwise specified, it is placed in the rest state.

The type of each circle, other than the center front and center far front circles, at the beginning of the game is a rear-guard type. If there are no cards or a face up card on those circles, they are rear-guard types.
When a card is moved to a rear-guard circle from anywhere other than another rear- guard circle, including a vanguard circle, it is put there in the stand state.

When a card is moved to a rear-guard circle from another rear-guard circle, it is put there in the same orientation state as the previous circle. “vanguard”, “rear-guard” or “guardian”, it refers to the unit on a circle of that type.
The type of circle with a locked card (7.30.1) on it is a lock circle.
Circles are public zones. The cards in these zones are face up, and all information is open to all players.
Cards that are face down on a circle due to effects or costs are still in a public zone. The information is open to all players.
Generally, only one card can be put on each vanguard, rear-guard, and lock circles. Multiple cards can be put on a guardian circle.

Other than moving G units not in the G zone between rear-guard circles, when a G unit that is not in the G zone moves to another area, after moving, or after finishing a chain of moving, that G unit is put back into the owner’s G zone in a face up state.
Circles can be classified as having the “Astral Plane” (17.3) type in addition to their other types.
Soul
Some cards will go into this zone during a game. The soul is not a part of the field.
Cards placed in the soul indicated as being in the soul by being stacked under the vanguard.
The soul is a public zone. Cards in this zone are stacked face up, and all information is open to all players. The order of the cards in the soul is not controlled.
Damage Zone
The zone you will put cards in as the game progresses to represent damage your vanguard has been dealt.
The damage zone is a public zone. Cards in this zone are stacked face up, and all information is open to all players. The order of the cards in the damage zone is not controlled.
Even if an effect or cost turns cards in a damage zone face down, they are still public information. Each player may see the face of the cards.
Cards that are face down in the damage zone do not have any card information and cannot be given any information.
If you have six or more cards in your damage zone, you lose the game by rule action (13.2.2).
Bind Zone
The zone that you put cards that have been bound.
The bind zone is a public zone. All players may see the information of face up cards in this zone.

Due to an effect, cards in the bind zone that are face up can be turned face down, and cards in other zones can be move to the bind zone face down. Only the owner of the face down cards in a bind zone may see the face. Other players may not see the face of these cards.
Bound cards that are faced down do not have any card information and cannot be given any information.

Bound cards or cards referring to bound cards may sometimes affect the game. As such, players are required to split the pile of bound cards so that they can be distinguished which effect they were bound by. You may change the order of your bound cards within the same pile.
Trigger Zone
The zone where cards are put in temporarily during the game.
Cards revealed by a drive check (10.6.1.2) are placed in the trigger zone. After resolving the effects of icons on it, the card moves to the owner's hand.
Cards revealed by a damage check (13.6.4) are placed in the trigger zone. After resolving the effects of icons on it, the card moves to the owner's damage zone.

The trigger zone is a public zone. All the cards in this zone are placed face up, and any player may see the information of these cards. The order of the cards in the trigger zone is controlled. When you put a card into this zone, put it on top of the existing cards.
G Zone
The zone you put your G deck in at the beginning of a game.

The G zone is a hidden zone, but you can see the information of cards in your G zone. The face down cards in this zone are stacked, and other players cannot see the information of the face down cards. The order of the cards in the G zone is not controlled.
At the beginning of a game, all cards in the G deck are placed face down on the G zone in a hidden state.

When cards in this zone are put to face up, they are placed separately from the face down cards, and only stacked with face up cards. All players can see the information of, and change the order of face up cards in the G zone.
When a process puts a card from outside of the G zone into the G zone during a game, that card is placed face up unless otherwise specified.
Gauge Zone
The zone where cards that are put as a gauge are placed.

The gauge zone is a hidden zone, but you can see the information of cards in your gauge zone. You may not see the information of cards in your opponent’s gauge zone. You may change the order of cards in your gauge zone, so long as it is clear which cards they are associated with.
When cards put into a gauge zone from a hidden zone, the owner of that gauge zone may look at the information of that card after all the cards have been put into the gauge zone.
There are cards in the gauge zone that are associated with players or other cards.
When a reference is made to a player’s or card’s “gauge”, it refers to the cards in the gauge zone that are associated that player or card.
When a unit is moved between circles, the cards in the gauge zone associated with that unit maintain the association.

When a unit is moved from a circle to a non-circle zone, or when a unit is locked (7.30), the cards in the gauge zone that are associated with that unit are placed into the drop zone by rule action (13.9.1).
The cards in a gauge zone that are associated with a unit can be referenced as part of the final information (11.13) of that unit, so long as they remain in the gauge zone.
When cards in the gauge zone that are associated with unit A become associated with a different unit B, their association with unit A is canceled.
There are cards in the gauge zone with name information.
References to “(name) gauge” refer to cards in the gauge zone with (name) in their name information.
Cards in the gauge zone that have not explicitly been given name information do not have any name information.
Order Area
The zone order cards are placed in while they are played (11.8.2.1.1).
The order area is a public zone. Cards are placed face up in this zone, and all players may check the information and order of those cards.
Order Zone
The zone set orders are placed in (11.8.3.3).
The order zone is a public zone, and all players may check the information of those cards.
Cards placed in the order zone have an orientation state and a facing state.
Cards that are face down in the order zone are considered to not have the information on its front side, unless otherwise specified.
Ride Deck Zone
The zone that players put their ride deck to differentiate it.

Face down cards in this zone are placed in a stack, and you cannot check the information of face down cards in other players’ ride deck zones. The order of the cards in the ride deck zone is not controlled.
At the beginning of the game, put all your ride deck cards in the ride deck zone face down in the hidden state.
When a card that was in the ride deck zone at the beginning of the game moves to the deck, that card is placed face up in the ride deck zone instead of the deck.

Face up cards in this zone are separated from the face down cards and placed in a stack that only has face up cards. All players may check the information and change the order of the face up cards in their ride deck zone.
Crest Zone
The zone where various crest markers created during a game are placed.
The crest zone is a public zone. Cards are placed face up in this zone, and all players may check the information of those cards.
Information
Information is any value, phrase, or icon that has any meaning or is referred to during a game. Information can be modified by some effects.

Information can be modified by some effects. If a card has multiple copies of the same information that are not abilities, the overlapping ones are ignored. - For example, if an effect that says “This card is also a <<Royal Paladin>>“ is applied to a unit that is already a <<Royal Paladin>>, then the second one is ignored, because it is multiple copies of the same information.
References to “original“ information refer to the information after effects that modify “original” information written on the card have been applied (11.11.1.2, 11.11.1.3).
References to the “original” information of a pseudo-card (15.1) are based on the information regulated by the effect or rule that created that pseudo-card.
State

State is another detail of cards other than information that can be referred during a game. - For example, a card being at rest is the state of being in the ‘rest state’, and is not information that the card possesses.
There are card effects that put some cards into a special ‘(name)’ state.
Cards with the card name specified by this effect are in the ‘(name)’ state in all zones.
Being put into this state may be referenced by other abilities and effects.
The (name) used for this rule is one of the following.  UnisonDress  Malwyrm
Overview
Units are placed on circles and gain special states through various methods during a game. This section defines the terms regarding the states of units.
Call
When a unit is placed by a call, that unit is placed on the specified rear-guard circle or guardian circle.
To “call” a unit is specific action that represents placing that unit by a call on the specified rear-guard circle or guardian circle.
Generally, if a unit is placed on a rear- guard circle or guardian circle, that unit is considered to have been “called” if it was not due to overDress (6.7.1).
Calls are divided into “normal calls” and “superior calls”.
A normal call is the placing of a unit on a rear-guard circle or guardian circle by the turn player playing a unit from their hand without any modifications to the cost by effects, than by an effect.
A superior call is the placing of a unit on a rear-guard circle or guardian circle that does not fulfill one or more of the conditions of a normal call.
When cards are called, it is done according to the steps below.
Choose the specified number of cards to call.
If the cards being called are cards in a hidden zone, the information of those cards is revealed.
For each of the cards being called, choose a circle for that card to be placed.

If multiple cards are being called at the same time due to an effect, choose cards and circles for placing such that it does not conflict with that effect or the conditions of the cards being called. When choosing, the same circle cannot be chosen as the destination to call to for multiple cards. They must be called to separate circles.

If there are not enough circles to call to for any reason, decide on a combination of units and circles that will allow as many cards as possible to be called. Cards that could not be included in that combination are not called, and remain in their original zone.
All the cards being called are placed on the circles at the same time.
Unless otherwise specified, called cards are placed in the stand state for rear- guard circles, and the rest state for the guardian circle.
If the circle the called unit on is a rear- guard circle, and that circle has a unit other than the unit that was called, the units on that circle other than the called unit are retired.

When units are called to the guardian circle, if any of those units’ master’s units is being attacked, that player chooses 1 of the units being attacked for each of the units called to the guardian circle.
While guardian units are on the guardian circle, the power of the unit being attacked that was chosen for those guardians is increased by the value of the shield of those guardians.
Cards that are called are considered as new cards in those zones. This includes when they are called from other circles, with 4.1.8 as an exception.
Ride
When a unit is placed by a ride, that unit is placed on the specified vanguard circle.
Rides are divided into “normal rides” and “superior rides”.
A normal ride is the placing of a unit on a vanguard circle by the turn player playing a unit from their hand or ride deck zone without any modifications to the cost by effects, than by an effect.
A superior ride is the placing of a unit on a vanguard circle that does not fulfill one or more of the conditions of a normal ride.
When cards are ridden, it is done according to the steps below.
If the cards being ridden are in the field or G zone, that ride is not performed, and the processing of the ride ends.
Choose the specified number of cards to ride.
If the cards being ridden are cards in a hidden zone, the information of those cards is revealed.
If the cards being ridden are cards in the ride deck zone, reveal that card. Then, if this ride is not by a card’s effect, you must choose a card from your hand and discard it.
Specify the vanguard circle to ride upon.
Unless otherwise specified, this circle is the vanguard circle of the owner of the cards being ridden.
Place the cards being ridden on the specified vanguard circle.
Unless otherwise specified, rode cards are placed in the stand state.
If there is another unit on the vanguard circle other than the rode unit, put all the units on that circle, other than the rode unit, into the soul.
Cards that would be put into by this include cards in the heart state (6.5.2.2) and legion leader and legion mate cards in the legion state (6.4).
Cards that are ridden are considered as new cards in that zone. This includes when they are ridden from another circle, with 4.1.8 as an exception.
Automatic abilities with the trigger condition of “when rode upon” are fulfilled when that unit is the vanguard and another card is placed on that vanguard circle by riding.

If a unit with a “when rode upon” ability moves to another public zone or changes to the public state in the zone it moved to, that unit can only be referred to in that zone. - For example, a vanguard has a “when rode upon, call this unit to a rear-guard circle” automatic ability. When this card is rode upon, if this card is put from the soul to the drop zone before this automatic ability is resolved, as the drop zone is not the zone it was put in immediately after being rode upon, this unit cannot be called from the drop zone.
When multiple cards with the same master are ridden at the same time, that master specifies an order for those cards, and rides one at a time in that order.
When you ride a card, if the card that was rode has an imaginary gift icon (2.13), perform the imaginary gift resolution (16.3) for the clan type indicated by that icon.

When you normal ride a card from hand, if the card currently placed on the vanguard circle has the same card name as the card being put on that circle from a ride, and both of them have the persona ride icon (2.13.3), that ride is considered a ‘persona ride’, and persona ride activates (7.15.1.4) as part of the ride process immediately after riding.
Legion
When instructed to “legion” a card with another card, it is done according to the steps below.
If that card is already in the legion state, that “legion” instruction is not performed, and the processing of the instruction ends.
Reveal the specified card in the specified zone as the card to be legioned with.
Put that card in the same zone and placement state as the card that was already present.
At this point, the card that was originally present and the card that was newly placed are given a “legion state” that associates them with one another.
Should either of the two units associated with one another through a legion state move to another zone or gain the heart state (6.5.2.2), the legion state of those two units ends.
Putting a new card on the vanguard circle from the processing of legion is not considered a ride (6.3).
Conditions that involve legion are defined as below.
“When (a card) legions” refers to when that card goes from not being in the legion state to being in the legion state.
“If (a card) is (in) legion” refers to whether that card is currently in the legion state.
“If (a card) legioned that turn” refers to whether that card went from not being in the legion state to being in the legion state during that turn.
While your vanguard is two cards in the legion state, one of them is called the “Legion Leader”, while the other that was newly placed is called the “Legion Mate”.
The Legion Leader and Legion Mate are determined when the legion process is performed.

If no mention is made regarding which card is to be the Legion Leader, the card with the Seek Mate ability (14.11) that has the name of the other card is the Legion Leader, and the other card is the Legion Mate.
Both the Legion Leader and Legion Mate are vanguards.
When the vanguard’s grade is referenced during the ride step as a condition for a normal ride, the Legion Leader’s grade is referenced.

When a vanguard in the legion state is attacked, only the Legion Leader is attacked. The Legion Mate cannot be attacked, and instructions to attack the Legion Mate and effects that force the Legion Mate to be attacked are not performed.
When either of the units in the legion state stands or rests, both units change to the same placement state.
If either of the units in the legion state is restricted from changing its placement state, both units are restricted from changing to the specified placement state.
Stride and Becoming a Heart
When instructed to “stride” a G unit, it is done according to the steps below.
Put the specified G unit card on the front row center vanguard circle, in the face up state and the same orientation state as the current vanguard.
Putting a new G unit on the vanguard circle from the processing of stride is not considered a ride (6.3).
All of the vanguards that were already on the front row center vanguard circle become hearts (6.5.2), and are associated with that G unit.

If the unit that became a heart is a G unit with heart cards associated with it, that association persists, and those associated heart cards also become associated with the new unit that was placed on the vanguard circle. Similarly, when a card in the heart state associated with other cards in the heart state becomes a G unit on that circle, the cards in the heart state associated with that card continue to be associated with that G unit.

Specify one of the cards in the heart state whose subtype is not “G” and is associated with that G unit. If that G unit is a vanguard and the specified card is in the heart state on this circle, that G unit gains the specified card’s card name, and the specified card’s power is added to its power.
Stride processes arising from stride skills that are not ultimate strides are called “normal strides”.
When a unit is instructed to “become a heart”, it is done according to the steps below.
Put the specified unit to the face up stand state.
That unit gains the “heart state” status.
While a unit has the “heart state”, that card is considered a “heart card”.
A card in the heart state loses the “unit” main type, and gains the “heart” main type.
Effects given to a unit do not apply to a card in the heart state, unless they are stated to apply to cards in the heart state in particular.
A card in the heart state remains on that circle, and only retains its power and card name. All its other information can only be referenced when another card refers to that information’s content.

When units in the legion state (6.4.1.3.1) becomes a heart, they maintain their legion state while becoming a heart. Similarly, when the heart state of two cards that are associated with each other through a legion state ends simultaneously, they maintain their legion state while their heart state ends, and return to being units.

At this point, should the unit information specified by one of the card’s seek mate ability (14.11) be fulfilled by the other card, that card with the seek mate ability becomes the legion leader, and the other card becomes the legion mate.

If the unit information specified by both cards’ seek mate abilities is fulfilled by the other card, specify one of those cards, and that card becomes the legion leader while the other becomes the legion mate.

If neither of the cards has the seek mate ability, or if neither of the cards fulfills the unit information specified by the other card’s seek mate ability, the legion state that associated the two cards with each other ends.
When a vanguard on a circle with cards in the heart state is rode (6.3) upon, all cards in the heart state are put into the soul.

If there is a card A that is in the heart state and a card B that was associated with A when A became a heart, and either card should move to another zone, it is done according to the steps below as appropriate for that movement.

When card B moves to another zone and card A is not associated with any other units or cards, the heart state of card A ends, put it to the same placement state as card B, and after its association with B ends, move it to card B’s zone.

If card B is associated with multiple cards in the heart state, choose a card with the subtype “G” from among those cards if there is one and any of those cards if there isn’t, and perform 6.5.4.1 with that card as card A.

When card A moves to another zone, if that card is the card specified in 6.5.1.3 when card B strode, immediately specify one of the cards in the heart state on that circle that does not have the subtype G, and consider it the card specified in 6.5.1.3. At this point, if the card in the heart state is not associated with card B, that card in the heart state becomes associated with card B.
Playing and Resolving Stride Skills
There are cards with the subtype G that have stride skills (14.12).

If it is currently the timing specified by the stride skill that is not an ultimate stride of a face down card in the G zone, and both players have a grade 3 or greater vanguard or your vanguard at the beginning of your turn was grade 3 or greater, that stride skill can be played and resolved according to the steps below.
Reveal the information of that card in the G zone.
Pay the cost specified by that stride skill.
Stride (6.5.1) that card on the vanguard in your front row center circle.

If it is currently the timing specified by the ultimate stride skill (14.13) of a Gyze card (17.2) or face down card in the G zone, and that card in the G zone has a nation that corresponds with the nations (2.14) of your front row center vanguard, that ultimate stride skill is played similarly to a stride skill, with the following exceptions.
If the front row center vanguard does not have nation information, you can only play the ultimate stride of units with the <Cray Elemental> race.
If the card being played is not a Gyze card (17.2), your G zone must have 3 or more face up cards to play it.
If the card being played is a Gyze card (17.2), one of your vanguards must be grade 3 or greater and your bind zone must have 5 or more different <Zeroth Dragon> to play it.
Ultimate stride skills are considered stride skills (14.12), but effects that change the cost needed for stride do not apply to the cost for ultimate stride.
When the G unit strode on the vanguard circle from ultimate stride returns to the G zone, all cards in the G zone are removed from the game upon it being returned to the G zone.
overDress
overDress is an action that puts a unit on a rear-guard circle.
The act of putting a unit on a rear-guard circle through overDress is not a call.
When instructed to “overDress” card A on unit B in a rear-guard circle, it is done according to the steps below.
The main type of unit B changes to “originalDress”.
Put card A on that rear-guard circle, and originalDress B is associated with unit A.
If originalDress B has originalDress cards associated with it, the association with unit B of all those associated cards is canceled, and become associated with unit A.
As long as a unit that was put on a rear-guard circle through overDress has originalDress associated with it, that unit is considered to be in the overDress state.
While a unit is associated with originalDress, that unit is considered the ‘outerDress’ for that originalDress.
When a card with originalDress cards associated with it moves to another zone, all originalDress cards associated with that card simultaneously move to that zone.

When a card with originalDress cards associated with it moves to a non-field zone, the association of all the originalDress cards associated with that card is canceled, and their main type becomes ‘unit’.

When a card with originalDress cards associated with it would move to the deck, if that card or any of the originalDress cards was in the ride deck zone at the beginning of the game, the cards that were in the ride deck zone are put face up into the ride deck zone instead of the deck (4.18.4).
XoverDress
XoverDress is an action that puts a unit on a rear-guard circle.
The act of putting a unit on a rear-guard circle through XoverDress is not a call.
The card that is to be placed on a rear-guard circle as a unit through XoverDress, and the series of rear-guards that becomes its originalDress, are specified for XoverDress.
When instructed to XoverDress card A on a specified rear-guard circle with cards with the specified conditions as originalDress, it is done according to the steps below.
Specify the required number of rear-guards that satisfy the conditions to become originalDress from your rear-guards.
Put all of the rear-guards specified in 6.8.3.1 on the specified circle, and their main type changes to “originalDress”.
Put card A on that rear-guard circle, and all the cards that became originalDress in 6.8.3.2 become associated with card A.
If there is a unit on this circle that are not originalDress associated with card A after the previous steps, that unit is put into the drop zone in the next rule action (13.3).
This unit A and all of the originalDress associated with it behave in accordance to the associated through overDress (6.7.3, 6.7.5).
As long as a unit that was put on a rear-guard through XoverDress has 1 or more originalDress associated with it, that unit is considered to be in the XoverDress state.
Placing through XoverDress is not placing through overDress. Similarly, units in the XoverDress state are not units in the overDress state.
Attach
Attach is a process that put a rear-guard on a vanguard circle and gives it the special type “attached”.
When there’s an instruction to “attach (unit A) to (unit B)”, perform the following steps.
If unit A is not a rear-guard, or unit B is not a vanguard, the performing of this instruction ends.
Move unit A to the circle unit B is on in the stand state, and unit A gets the special type “attached”.
Unit A becomes associated with unit B.
While a unit has the special type “attached”, the following are applicable.
An attached unit is not considered a vanguard, even though it is on the vanguard circle.
An attached unit cannot attack, and cannot become the unit being attacked.
All of the abilities of an attached unit are nullified.
The vanguard associated with an attached unit gets all of the abilities of that attached unit., and its power is increased by a value equal to the power of that attached unit.
This modification is a modification of effects (11.11.1.4).
The vanguard associated with an attached unit has its power increased by a value equal to the power of that attached unit (11.11.1.8).
Depending on the situation, the illegal attached card rule action (13.12) may be applied to an attached unit.
An attached card is moved to a rear-guard circle of the player’s choice in the rest state at the end phase.
Overview
Specific actions are states or instructions of actions that have a special meaning when playing this game.
Stand/Rest
When instructed to “stand” or “rest” a card, change the orientation of the specified card to the stand state or rest state in accordance with the instruction.
Turn Face Up/Face Down
When instructed to “turn (card) face up” or “turn (card) face down”, change the facing of the specified card to face up or face down in accordance with the instruction.
Put
When instructed to “put” a card into a specified zone, move that card to that zone.
When instructed to “put a (name) marker” on a circle, create a marker with name (name) on that circle.
Shuffle
When instructed to “shuffle” a deck, the player that deck belongs to randomizes the order of the cards in that deck.
When instructed to shuffle a deck that has 0 cards or 1 card, the order of the cards in that deck is not changed, but the shuffle is considered to have been performed.
Move Cards from the Deck/Draw
When instructed to move a card from the deck, the specified player moves the top card of the deck to the specified zone.
When instructed to “move (number) cards” from the deck, the specified player repeats the moving of one card (number) times.
When instructed to “move up to (number) cards” from the deck, the specified player performs the following steps.
If (number) is 0 or less, nothing is done and the performing of that instruction ends.
The specified player can end the performing of this instruction.
The specified player moves 1 card.
If the number of times 7.6.3.3 has been performed for this instruction has reached (number) times, the performing of this instruction ends. If it has not, return to 7.6.3.2.
When instructed to “draw” cards, perform the process listed above to move cards from the deck to your hand.
“Drawing cards by a card’s ability” refers to all acts of drawing cards other than by the process of drawing cards during a normal draw phase (9.4.2).
The processes of drawing cards by trigger effects (11.10.4), Accel II (16.3.1.5.4), and Persona Ride (7.15.1.4) are included in “drawing cards by a card’s ability”.
Look at the Deck
When instructed to “look at (number) cards from the top of the deck”, the specified player can check the information of the top (number) cards of that deck.
When instructed to “look at up to (number) cards from the top of the deck”, perform the following steps.
If (number) is 0 or less, nothing is done and the performing of this instruction ends.
Specify a number X with the value of 1. If not, add 1 to the number X.
The specified player can end the performing of this instruction.
The specified player can check the information of the card that is the specified number of cards from the top of the deck.
If the number of times 7.7.2.4 has been performed for this instruction has reached (number) times, the performing of this instruction ends. If it has not, add 1 to X and return to 7.7.2.3.

If a continuous ability is deemed to allow a portion of the cards in the deck to be looked at without specifying any particular timing to do so, the information of those cards can be checked whenever you wish.

When checking the information of cards with such an ability, so long as the positions of those cards within the deck have not been changed, the “look” action is considered to have only been performed one time, regardless of the number of times that information is checked.

When an effect looks at cards from a deck multiple times in a single effect, an automatic ability that has looking at cards from the deck as a trigger condition will only trigger the first time the deck was looked at, and does not trigger for the second time the deck was looked at in the same effect and onwards.
Switch
When instructed to “switch” a card and another card, move the former card to the latter card’s zone and the latter card to the former’s card zone simultaneously.
If either of the cards is unable to move to the other’s zone at the point of performing the instruction to switch for any reason, that instruction is not performed.
When text requires you to “switch” zones A and B, the cards in zone A and the cards in zone B move to each other’s zones simultaneously.
Discard
“To discard“ is a specific action to move a card from its owner’s deck or hand or gauge zone to that player’s drop zone.
When a card is put into the drop zone from the deck, hand, or gauge zone, that card is considered to have been discarded.
Reveal
“To reveal“ is a specific action to show cards to all players for a certain time.
When instructed by an effect “to show” cards, it means “to reveal” them.
When revealing cards as a cost, decide all costs first, and reveal the applicable cards when all costs are simultaneously paid (11.7.1).
If an effect asks you to reveal cards, then show them until the end of the effect.
Cards return to being hidden after the end of the revealing period.
Revealing cards do not change the zones that they are in.
Search
“To search“ is a specific action to look at all the cards in an applicable zone or range, and find the applicable cards.
If the “search” zone is a hidden zone, you can choose not to find the cards even if applicable cards exist.
If the “search” zone is a public zone, you must find the cards if applicable cards exist.
When instructed to “search (zone A) and (zone B)”, you can search both zones.
Shuffle
“To shuffle“ is a specific action to randomize the order of cards in an applicable hidden zone.
When an instruction “to shuffle“ follows an instruction “to search”, unless otherwise specified, the card that was found is not randomized, while the rest of the cards are randomized.

When shuffling, even if the cards in the applicable hidden zone are in the public state or any player is able to look at them due to an effect, all those cards are in the hidden state while shuffling, and neither player can look at them.
Declare
“To declare“ is a specific action to specify special information a card has.
When declaring information, you must specify appropriate information. - For example, when “declaring“ a card name, you must specify an existing card, and it must uniquely identify the specified card.
Give/Lose/Get
“To give” or “get” abilities is a specific action that considers the applicable card to have the applicable ability indicated by text or skill icon for the specified period.
“To lose” abilities is a specific action that considers the applicable card to not have the applicable ability indicated by text or skill icon for the specified period.
When a player “gets a (specified clan type’s imaginary gift)”, perform the imaginary gift resolution (16.3) for the specified clan type.
This process is performed immediately without waiting for the check timing.
If the player that gets the imaginary gift from the imaginary gift resolution is not stated, the master of that effect gets the imaginary gift.

When card A with numerical information “gets” that numerical information from card B that has the same type of numerical information, the value of that numerical information of card B is added to that numerical information of card A.
When a player “gets a (specified) crest”, create 1 of the specified crest in the crest zone belonging to that player.
Activate
If a card text says that an ability will activate, its meaning depends on the category of the ability.
Activating a continuous ability means that that continuous ability is in effect.
Activating an activated ability means to play and resolve that activated ability.
Activating an automatic ability means that automatic ability’s trigger condition is fulfilled and becomes standby.

“Activate (a specific) automatic ability (number) of times” means that when that automatic ability is played, if the number of times that ability has been played for that standby state has not yet reached (number) times, that standby state is not canceled (11.9.4).
“(Automatic) abilities do not activate” for a special situation means that automatic abilities with that special situation as a trigger condition do not become standby from that situation.
Activating “persona ride” means the player specified by that process performs the following.
That player draws a card.
Until the end of the turn, that player’s units get Power +10000 while they are on that player’s front row circles.
Activating any other process that is not an ability means to perform that process.
(Trigger Unit) is Revealed
“(Trigger unit) is revealed” means that that trigger unit card is put in the trigger zone by a drive check (10.6.1.2) or damage check (13.6.4).
Place
“To place” is a specific action to move a card from anywhere that is not a circle to a circle.
Regardless of whether a unit was played, if it is put on a circle from anywhere that is not a circle, or it is put on the circle from a call or ride, it is considered to have been “placed”.
Retire
“To retire“ is a specific action to move a card from the field to its owner’s drop zone.
When a unit is put into the drop zone from the field, that unit is considered to have been retired.
Remove
When the text requires you “to remove“ cards, those cards will be removed from the game, and no longer exist within the game.
The information of removed cards is public information.
Heal
“To heal“ is a specific action to move a card from your damage zone to your drop zone.
Losing cost
To “lose” cost is a specific action where for the specified period, when the cost for the applicable ability is to be paid, the actions indicated by the cost are not performed.
(Perform) Drive Check
Drive check is a specific action that indicates the series of operations (10.6) in the drive step (10.6.1.2.3).
(Perform) Damage Check
Damage check is a specific action that indicates the series of operations performed when vanguard damage is 1 or higher (13.6.3).
Counter-blast
Counter-blast is a specific action to choose the specified number of face up cards in the damage zone and turn them face down. This is indicated by the or icons.
When written as [(counter-blast icon)(number in a circle)], choose the specified number of face up cards in the damage zone and turn them face down.

When written as [(counter-blast icon)(number in a circle)-(condition)], choose the specified number of face up cards in the damage zone that fulfill the condition written after the “-“ and turn them face down.

When written as an instruction to “(counter- blast icon)(number in a circle)” as part of an effect instead of the cost, the player specified by that effect or the master of the specified card chooses face up cards in their damage zone equal to the number in the circle, and turns them face down. If the specified number of face up cards cannot be chosen, that instruction is not performed.
“To counter-blast” is to turn face up cards in the damage zone face down by counter-blast.
“To counter-blast (number)” is to turn that number of face up cards in the damage zone face down by counter-blast.
Soul-blast
Soul-blast is a specific action to choose the specified number of cards in the soul and put them into the drop zone. This is indicated by the or icons.
When written as [(soul-blast icon)(number in a circle)], choose the specified number of cards in the soul and put them into the drop zone.
When written as [(soul-blast icon)(number in a circle)-(condition)], choose the specified number of cards in the soul that fulfill the condition written after the “-“ and put them into the drop zone.

When written as an instruction to “(soul-blast icon)(number in a circle)” as part of an effect instead of the cost, the player specified by the effect or the master of the specified card chooses cards in their soul equal to the number in the circle, and puts them into the drop zone. If the specified number of cards cannot be chosen, that instruction is not performed.
“To soul-blast” is to put cards from the soul into the drop zone by soul-blast.
“To soul-blast (number)” is to put that number of cards from the soul into the drop zone by soul-blast.
Counter-charge

Counter-charge is indicated by an icon like “ (1)“ or “ “. It is a specific action to choose a number of the face down cards in the damage zone equal to the number in the circle and turn them face up.
“To counter-charge” is to turn face down cards in the damage zone face up by counter-- charge.
“To counter-charge (number)” is to turn that number of face down cards in the damage zone face up by counter -charge.
Soul-charge
Soul-charge is indicated by an icon like “ (1)“ or “ “, and is a specific action to put a number of cards equal to the number in the circle from the top of the deck into the soul.
“To soul-charge” is to put cards from the top of the deck into the soul by soul-charge.
“To soul-charge (number)” is to put that number of cards from the top of the deck into the soul by soul-charge.
Increase / Decrease

If the number denoted in an icon such as for counter-blast is “increased” or “decreased”, it means that the number referenced when performing the action indicated by that icon is increased or decreased by the specified number.

When a process increases or decreases the number for the “next time” of a process, that number is increased or decreased the next time that process is performed. This is regardless of whether other processes are performed before that next time.
If there are multiple processes that increase or decrease the number for the “next time” of the same process, they are added together.
Bind
“To bind” is a specific action to move cards from a specified zone to the owner’s bind zone.
Lock
“To lock” is a specific action to change the state of a card. By locking a card, the card changes to the locked state.
When a card changes to the locked state, it is faced down, and then put in the stand state. This card is not considered to be the same card as the original card.
A card that changes to the locked state becomes a “locked card”. Locked cards are a type of card, and do not have all the information that is written on the front side, given to it, or gained.
When whether a locked card is in the stand state or rest state is referenced, it is neither in the stand state or rest state, and cannot be referenced.

When a card that is locked changes state to no longer being so, it is turned face up. Similarly, when a card that is locked is turned face up for any reason, it is no longer in the locked state, and is considered to have been unlocked (7.31). In both cases, the lock type circle that card is on returns to its original type.
A circle is a lock type circle so long as a locked card is on it.
When a lock type circle’s type is no longer the lock type, that circle returns to its original type unless stated otherwise.
When a G unit on a rear-guard circle is locked, right after that card is turned face down, put that card into its owner’s G zone face up.
When instructed to “put as a locked card”, that card is not a unit when it is put and is put face down as a locked card.

When a card is “put as a locked card” from a hidden zone such as the deck, that card’s owner checks the information of that card before deciding the circle to put it unless instructed otherwise by an effect.

When the rear-guard circle a unit or card is on becomes a lock type circle by something like “put as a locked card”, the units and cards that were there are immediately put into their owner’s drop zones without waiting for the check timing.

When multiple locked cards simultaneously put on circles, choose circles for them to be put in a manner that does not contradict the conditions. At that point, you cannot choose the same circle as the circle to put multiple locked cards. You must choose separate circles to put them on.
A card in the locked state does not reference any other card.

When a unit is locked, if that unit has an associated originalDress card (6.7.2.2), that originalDress card is associated with that locked card. Similarly, when a card in the locked state changes state to no longer being so, if that card in the locked state has an associated originalDress card, that originalDress card is associated with that card that is no longer in the locked state.
Unlock
“To unlock“ is a specific action to change the state of a card. By unlocking a card, if it is in the locked state, the card is turned face up from the locked state.
An unlocked card is not considered to be the same as the original card.
When unlocked, the card is in the stand state. This is not considered as changing to the stand state from the rest state, and abilities and effects that have changing to the stand state do not apply.
If a locked card is turned face up for any reason, it is considered to have been unlocked.
The unlocking of a card is not a place.
Delete
When a unit changes to the deleted state, it is turned face down while its orientation state is maintained. This unit is considered to be the same as the original unit.

A unit that changes to the deleted state is a “deleted unit“. Deleted units are a type of unit, but its power is reduced by the power written on the card, and it loses the text that is written on the face up side. Skill icons and other card information are maintained. - For example, when a “King of Knights, Alfred“ vanguard that gets +2000 power from the ability of “Starlight Unicorn“ is deleted, its power becomes 2000. Also, since it has no text, it can be boosted.
Deleted units have stand/rest states, and battles as a unit that is not deleted would.
When a deleted unit changes state to no longer being so, the unit is turn faced up. Similarly, when a deleted unit is turned face up for any reason, it is no longer in a deleted state.
All players can check the face up side of a deleted unit.

When a deleted unit is given or gets an ability, it is given or gets the ability as per normal. Similarly, when a deleted unit has its power increased or decreased, it is increased or decreased as per normal.

If a deleted unit has its information modified by any continuous effect, and is no longer in a deleted state during the duration of that continuous effect, that modification continues to be in effect.
When a unit in a legion state is deleted, that legion state is maintained.
When a deleted unit is rode upon, all the vanguards on that circle at that point in time are put into the soul face up.
Time Leap
“To time leap“ is a special action that is performed according to the process below.

When “time leap“ is performed, bind the chosen rear-guards if a rear-guard was chosen, or that unit itself if it was chosen. If cards were bound, for each card that was bound, search your deck for up to one card with grade 1 grade greater than that card and associate them, call all of the cards associated with the cards that were bound at the same time they were associated, and shuffle your deck. At the end of that turn, put that called unit on the bottom of its owner’s deck. If it was put, the owner of the card associated with that unit and bound by time leap calls it.
Move/Put a Unit
When “move“ or “put a unit that was already in the field on a specific circle“ is written in text, it refers to a unit put within the field being put on another circle within the field.
When intercepting or exchanging the position of cards placed on circles, with regards to the text, the cards are considered as being moved.
With regards to the text, riding and calling units are not considered as moving.
Dealing Damage
When a rule or text “deals (number) damage“ to a vanguard, increase that vanguard’s master’s vanguard damage by that specified number.
When instructed to deal damage to the vanguard with the number of vanguards being specified, if there are multiple vanguards, deal the specified damage to each of those vanguards.
The resolution for the damage dealt by this is performed within a rule action (13.6).
Attack
When there is an instruction “(unit A) attacks (unit B)“ in text, after performing the check timing effect currently being performed, perform the following process.

Specify one unit in the stand state that is not restricted from attacking by effects from the units specified as unit A as the attacking unit, and specify one unit that is not restricted from being attacked by effects from the units specified as unit B as the unit being attacked. If such a combination cannot be specified, the attack special action ends.
Perform an attack resolution (10.2). No boosting unit (10.4.1.12) can be specified for this attack resolution. Then, return to 7.36.1.1.
For this attack resolution, the master of the effect with the instruction to attack is the designated attacking player, and unit B’s master is the designated defending player (10.1.6).
After the battle has begun, if there is an instruction during that battle to “attack a unit“ in the text, process that “attack a unit” after the ongoing battle has ended.

When there is an instruction for multiple units to attack, if there are units whose master is the turn player among them, the turn player chooses one of the units they are the master of from among them, and if not, the non-turn player chooses one of the units they are the master of from among them, and performs the instruction to attack, and this is repeated until there are no more units directed to attack.
If there are processes following the instruction to attack that reference “that attack”, it refers to the battle from the attack process performed from that instruction to attack.
Battle
“To battle” is a specific action to change the unit being attacked (10.4.1.8).
Changing of (Attack Target)
When there is an instruction to “change the attack target (to a specified unit)” for an attacking unit, the specified unit being attacked (10.2.2) by that attacking unit becomes that specified unit.

When any effect changes the attack target of a unit that is attacking multiple units to a specified unit, the specified unit being attacked for those attacking units changes to only be that specified unit.
Dominate
When text says to “dominate“ a unit, the master of the effect with that text is temporarily able to use that unit as if they were that unit’s master.

While being able to use that unit as if you were its master from this, that unit has a “dominated state” from that effect’s master, and that master is considered to be that unit’s “dominating player”. The master of that unit before it was in the dominated state is written as the “original master”.
While in the dominated state, the original master cannot refer to the dominated unit as a unit they are the master of.
A unit in dominated state cannot further change to the dominated state.
If the duration it is dominated is not mentioned, that card will only be in the dominated state while the effect with the “dominate” action Is being resolved.
If a specified card is dominated and put on the guardian circle, that card will be in the dominated state until the end of that battle.

When a unit in the dominated state refers to its master at a specified later time, that unit will confirm its master when that time arrives, and refer to them. As a result, it may refer to a player that is not the dominating player. - For example, when a rear-guard in the dominated state applies a ”does not stand in your next stand phase” effect, and it is no longer in the dominated state at a later time during that turn, that rear-guard does not stand during its original master’s next stand phase.
If either a legion leader or legion mate in the legion state changes to the dominated state, the unit associated with it changes to the dominated state.

When referring to the units the dominating player is the master of, units in the dominated state are included. Similarly, when a unit in the dominating state refers to its master or their information, it refers to the dominating player or their information.
When referring to the number of units the dominating player is the master of, units in dominated state are included.
Effects applied by units the dominating player is the master of are applied to units in the dominated state.
The dominating player can play the abilities of units in dominated state as if they were its master.

When a unit in the dominated state creates an automatic ability with a timed trigger (11.9.7), when that timed trigger’s condition is fulfilled, the dominating player at the point that automatic ability was created plays that ability.
When a unit in the dominated state is locked, it is no longer in dominated state.

After a unit the dominating player is the master of is moved to a deck that is not the dominating player’s deck by any effect, when there is an instruction to shuffle the dominating player’s deck during that effect, all players shuffle their decks.
The positions of units in the dominated state are based on the dominating player.

When a rear-guard in your opponent’s right column is dominated, it becomes a rear- guard in the dominating player’s left column, and is considered to be in the same column as the other rear-guards in the dominating player’s left column. It is similar for the opponent’s left column.
Although circles with different masters may be in the same column, they do not regard each other as being the other’s front or back row.

When a dominating player references “your front row units” or “your back row units”, it does not include dominated units. Similarly, when the original master references “your front row units” or “your back row units”, it does not include dominated units.
When a unit in the dominated state moves to another zone by rule or effect, it does so in
When that is a move to a non-circle zone, it moves to that card’s owner’s specified zone.
When that is a move to another rear- guard circle or vanguard circle, if that circle’s master is different from that unit’s owner, that move is not performed.
If it does not meet the above conditions, that move is processed according to the
The master of the circle a unit in the dominated state is on does not change.
When a unit whose owner is different from the master of the circle a unit in the dominated state is on is called to or rode upon that circle, it is not performed.
A rear-guard in the dominated state cannot boost nor intercept.
When a vanguard in the dominated state attacks, drive checks for the drive step are performed by putting cards from the top of the dominating player’s deck into the dominating player’s trigger zone.
If the circle a dominated unit is on was specified for any imaginary gift process, the modifications applied to that circle are not applied.
Put as gauge/Put as plant gauge/Move gauge
When a card is to be “put as gauge” by text, move that card to its owner’s gauge zone (4.15).
When card A is to be “put as gauge” for card B, in addition to putting card A as gauge, that card is associated with card B (4.15.3).
If card A and card B have different owners or masters, that “put as gauge” action is not performed.
When a card is to be “put as (name) gauge” by text, in addition to putting that card as gauge, that card gains (name) as name information (4.15.4).

If multiple gauges are being put in as single process, after choosing the number to be put if there is a choice of quantity, move the specified or chosen number of cards to the gauge zone. - For example, when the single process “put up to three cards from the top of your deck as gauge” is resolved with “two cards”, move 2 cards from the deck as “two cards” was decided. You may not look at the information of the first card before deciding whether to put a second card.

When there’s an instruction to “put a token as a plant gauge”, the gauge zone is added to that token’s effective zones (15.2.4.1), the gauge zone is removed from that token’s erase zones (15.2.4.2), and that token is put as gauge.

When “move gauge” is performed on a card in a gauge, that card’s association with the card it is currently associated with is canceled, and it becomes associated with the card specified as the move destination.
Cards in the gauge do not change zone from the move gauge process.
If the card specified as the move destination and the gauge card being moved have different owners or masters, that “move gauge” action is not performed.
When there’s an instruction to put a card as a player’s gauge, perform the following process.
If there is no effect applied to that player that allows them to have that gauge, do nothing for this process.
If there is an effect applied to that player that allows them to have that gauge, that card is put as gauge, and that card is associated with that player (4.15.3).
Become the Stage
When there is an instruction for a circle to “become the stage” in text, perform the following.
If that circle does not have the “stage” type, it additionally gains the “stage” type.
If there are clan type “Accel” gift markers on any circles other than that circle, move them all to that circle.
The circles the gift markers moved by this were on will disappear (16.3.1.5.2.1).

If there is a circle that is the “stage”, when the clan type “Accel” imaginary gift process is performed, no new circles are created, and the gift marker from that process is put on the circle that is the “stage” (16.3.1.5.2).
“Final Rush”/”Final Burst”
When any player is instructed to “Final Rush” or “Final Burst”, that player is considered to be “in Final Rush” or “in Final Burst” for the specified duration.
Players that are “in Final Burst” are simultaneously “in Final Rush”.
“Final Rush” and “Final Burst” have no referenced by other effects.
World/Becomes Dark Night/Becomes Abyssal Dark Night
Each player has “world” information.
So long as there are no effects that determine a player’s world information, they are in a state of having a blank value for their world information.
There are effects that have the information of the world “become Dark Night” or “become Abyssal Dark Night”.
When a player’s world becomes a specified information, the world information it had until then is lost, and it only has the new information.
World information has no particular meaning effects.
